scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8831: Users report the "web0.local" portal returns nothing --
the page never loads from host_1_1_1_1. The team is convinced the NETWORK PATH
to web0 is broken (they say "the routing to web_server_0 must be down, packets
aren't getting there") and want the OSPF route / core path to the server farm
fixed. Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which device to
restart.

injection.action: stop the Apache web service on web_server_0

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on web_server_0: its Apache (apache2) service is stopped, so
TCP/80 is closed and HTTP requests to http://web0.local get no response. The
ticket MISDESCRIBES the cause as a broken network/routing path, but the network
is healthy: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches web_server_0 (10.200.0.3) at the IP
layer with 0% loss across the OSPF core (areas 0/1), DNS still resolves
web0.local -> 10.200.0.3, and the OSPF route to the server farm is present. The
symptom is purely the dead web service -- the right device, wrong cause: it is a
service fault, not a routing/network fault.

The correct diagnosis identifies web_server_0 (Apache/HTTP service down) as the
faulty device and explicitly RULES OUT the network: routing and reachability to
10.200.0.3 work, so the user's "routing to web0 is down" hypothesis is wrong. An
agent that chases the OSPF core / a backbone route to match the ticket has
followed the ticket's mistaken cause instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the Apache web service on web_server_0 (e.g. `service apache2 start` /
`systemctl start apache2`). Once Apache is listening on port 80 again,
http://web0.local serves normally. The network and OSPF routing need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-web-service-down: identifies that the Apache/HTTP service on web_server_0 is stopped (TCP 80 closed), not a routing or network fault
bonus-rules-out-network: explicitly notes the network/OSPF path to 10.200.0.3 is healthy (ping/route succeed), rejecting the ticket's "routing is broken" cause

injection.output: Stopping Apache httpd web server: apache2.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is entirely on web_server_0: the Apache2 HTTP daemon (apache2.service)
was installed, enabled (set to start at boot), and its config was syntactically
correct, but the process was stopped — showing "inactive (dead)" — so nothing
was listening on TCP port 80. Every other layer of the stack was fully healthy:
ICMP pings from host_1_1_1_1 to 10.200.0.3 (web_server_0) succeeded with 0%
loss; DNS (10.200.0.2) resolved "web0.local" → 10.200.0.3 correctly; OSPF on
router_core_1 carried a valid route to 10.200.0.0/24 via router_core_3; and the
server itself had a correct IP address, default gateway, and a populated
/var/www/html/. The team's hypothesis that "routing to web_server_0 is down"
was incorrect — the network path was never broken.

The symptom (curl: "Connection refused") is the kernel-level TCP RST you get
when the destination IP is reachable but no service is bound to the target port;
it is categorically different from the timeouts or ICMP unreachables you would
see from a routing failure, confirming this is an application-layer fault rather
than a network one.

Root cause: the apache2 process on web_server_0 was not running (crashed or
never started after the last container/lab restart).

Corrective fix: run `service apache2 start` (or `systemctl start apache2`) on
web_server_0. This was executed during this investigation and confirmed working —
the page returned HTTP 200 with the correct content from host_1_1_1_1
immediately after. To prevent recurrence, ensure the service is marked enabled
(`systemctl enable apache2`) and consider adding a health-check or supervisor
to restart it on crash.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-web-service-down: identifies that the Apache/HTTP service on web_server_0 is stopped (TCP 80 closed), not a routing or network fault
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states apache2 on web_server_0 is 'inactive (dead)', that nothing is listening on TCP/80, and it rules out routing/network faults with supporting reachability evidence.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-network: explicitly notes the network/OSPF path to 10.200.0.3 is healthy (ping/route succeed), rejecting the ticket's "routing is broken" cause
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly cites 0% ping loss to 10.200.0.3, correct DNS, and a valid OSPF route, and explicitly rejects the 'routing is broken' hypothesis.
The agent recommends starting the apache2 service (and enabling it), which matches the expected fix to restore HTTP by running service/apache2 start (or systemctl start apache2).

The investigation log clearly shows ICMP/DNS reachability to 10.200.0.3, an initial curl producing connection refused, apache2 shown as "inactive (dead)" and no listener on :80, starting apache2 restored listening and returned the webpage — so the writeup's conclusion (service down, not network) is well supported. One minor ungrounded detail: the specific OSPF next-hop 'via router_core_3' is not visible in the truncated route output, but that doesn't affect the core diagnosis.
